Three more records of ours, same pattern, found after the issue was opened:

**GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-021897 — helios-broadcast 0.2.0.** P-CRON-CREATE and P-LOG-CLEAR match the
install instructions in `README.md` (a cron line that runs `docker exec helios helios worker`
hourly and appends to its own log file). P-PASSWD-READ matches `"path": "/etc/passwd"` in
`tests/test_calliope.py`, a test input.

**GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-021896 — skopos-fleet 0.2.0.** P-SSH-ACCESS matches `key_path: ~/.ssh/id_rsa`
in the configuration guide (`docs/*/guide/configuration.md`), an example of where the operator's
own key is. P-DNS-EXFIL matches an nginx `log_format` line in the same guide.

**GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-022091 — aimarket-histor 0.2.0.** P-XDG-AUTOSTART matches the `PERSIST` tuple
in `sandbox/histor_observe.py`: the list of persistence locations HISTOR's sandbox observer
*watches* when it runs third-party packages, to report packages that write there.

Please withdraw these three with the other six.

Reviewed all six artifacts. No malicious behaviour found in any of them.

**Withdrawn**, with an OpenVEX `not_affected` statement:
- GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-020949 (aimarket-hestia-agents): https://github.com/Vulnetix/advisory-database/blob/main/openvex/PYPI/2026/20xxx/GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-020949.openvex.json

**Reclassified from malware to a vulnerability**, under the same ids:

| Record | Package | CWE | CVSS 3.1 | Versions | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-018883 | aimarket-mcp | CWE-306 | 6.5 | 0.1.0–0.6.0 | `_auth_ok` accepts every request when `AIMARKET_MCP_KEY` is unset, and the server binds 0.0.0.0 |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-021807 | aimarket-emporion | CWE-693 | 6.5 | 0.1.0, 0.4.0 | `parse_ofac` never reads OFAC `SDN_COMMENTS.CSV`, so 538 listed wallet addresses screen as not listed |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-004375 | aimarket-hub | CWE-918 | 5.4 | 3.0.0, fixed in 3.1.0 | the federated invoke posts to a peer-supplied `mcp_endpoint` without validating it |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-021946 | aimarket-signal-hunt | CWE-918 | 4.0 | 0.1.0–0.1.1 | the peer probe re-resolves the host after its IP check (0.1.0 has no check) |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-020712 | aimarket-hestia | CWE-863 | 3.1 | 0.1.0–0.1.1 | a stored `may_run_code` granted under the WASM runtime still applies after a switch to the stub runtime |

Correction to the report: hestia's `exec` runs under WASI/wasmtime, not gVisor.

Thank you very much — for reviewing all six by hand, for withdrawing -020949 with an OpenVEX statement,
and for turning the other five into precise vulnerability records. You read the code more closely than we
had, and you were right on all five. One was serious: our OFAC screen missed more than half of the listed
wallets, so it could say "not listed" for a listed address. Thank you for catching it.

All five are fixed:

- **-021807, aimarket-emporion 0.4.1.** `SDN_COMMENTS.CSV` is fetched with the SDN list and joined to
  each remark before addresses are read (OFAC's cut can fall inside an address). A list load fails without
  it, and a list cached by 0.4.0 is not served. On today's lists that is 1,050 addresses instead of 499.
- **-018883, aimarket-mcp 0.6.1.** The HTTP server binds `127.0.0.1` by default. Without a key it answers
  only callers on the machine itself (a loopback packet with a loopback `Host`, no forwarding headers, no
  cross-site `Origin`), unless `AIMARKET_MCP_PUBLIC=1` opens it on purpose.
- **-021946, aimarket-signal-hunt 0.1.2.** The probe connects to the address that passed the check, with
  the peer's name in `Host` and TLS SNI, so the certificate is still verified against it. Connections are
  not kept alive between probes, and IPv6 forms that carry a private IPv4 (NAT64, 6to4) are refused.
- **-020712, aimarket-hestia 0.1.2.** It was wider than the stored flag: after a switch to the stub
  runtime a restart also brought an open-signup key's handlers back as plain child processes, and an
  operator's routine update of such a key wrote the right again. One rule now decides it everywhere: an
  open-signup key runs code only in the wasm sandbox, whatever is stored. Owner updates change only the
  fields they name, and taking a right away stops the owner's running handlers at once.
- **-004375, aimarket-hub: agreed, with one correction to the range.** The PyPI wheels show 3.1.0 still
  posting to the advertised endpoint (for oracle-like peers), and 3.2.0 and 3.2.1 doing so for every peer.
  The same-origin check first shipped in **3.7.0**, so it is affected 3.0.0–3.2.1, fixed in 3.7.0.

Your correction stands: a HESTIA owner's handler runs under WASI/wasmtime; gVisor isolates image tenants.
Our first message had that wrong.

Could you set the fixed versions on the records (emporion 0.4.1, mcp 0.6.1, signal-hunt 0.1.2,
hestia 0.1.2, and hub 3.7.0 with the range above)? And, when you have time, the three later records from
my comment above (-021897, -021896, -022091) are still listed as malware.

Before writing this we had the fixes re-checked by a separate reviewer (an AI agent given only the code
and your findings, not our reasoning). It found gaps our first fix left in hestia and aimarket-mcp; they
are closed in the same releases.

For transparency: we are writing up a comparison of open malware feeds, and your database is one of the
feeds in it. Your answer here will be reported as you gave it, together with these fixes.

Thanks again.

the poc will not be published in GitHub, please review the VDP on our website if you require a PoC.
the triage and report tool has messed up the identifier casting. apologies.
the additional 3 were queued and will have a human review shortly.

Reviewed the three later records and checked each fix against the published wheels.

**Reclassified from malware to a vulnerability**, under the same ids. No malicious behaviour in any of them:

| Record | Package | CWE | CVSS 3.1 | Versions | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-021897 | helios-broadcast | CWE-863 | 4.4 | 0.1.0–0.2.0 | `worker.process_job` takes `privacy` from the queued job's `youtube` object, which `ingest_external_queue` copies unvalidated from the shared queue file, so a queue producer can publish a video as public without `helios approve` |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-021896 | skopos-fleet | CWE-295, CWE-307 | 4.8 | 0.1.0–0.2.0 | `ssh.run_command` accepts any host key by default (`AutoAddPolicy`, no known_hosts) in 0.1.0–0.1.4; the login lockout is keyed on a client-supplied header (`X-Real-IP` in 0.2.0, left-most `X-Forwarded-For` in 0.1.5) |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-022091 | aimarket-histor | CWE-693 | 5.3 | 0.2.0–0.3.1 | the sandbox trace leaves out `rename`, `renameat2`, `link`, `symlink` and `creat`, so a file renamed onto `.bashrc` is not reported and the run is marked complete; writes under `/work` (e.g. a `.pth` file) are never reported |

**Fixed versions set**, each verified in the published wheel:

| Record | Package | Affected | Fixed |
|---|---|---|---|
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-021807 | aimarket-emporion | 0.1.0, 0.4.0 | 0.4.1 |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-018883 | aimarket-mcp | 0.1.0–0.6.0 | 0.6.1 |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-021946 | aimarket-signal-hunt | 0.1.0–0.1.1 | 0.1.2 |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-020712 | aimarket-hestia | 0.1.0–0.1.1 | 0.1.2 |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-004375 | aimarket-hub | 3.0.0–3.2.1 | 3.7.0 |

The aimarket-hub range correction is right. One detail: 3.2.0 still follows the endpoint only for oracle-like peers; 3.2.1 is the first to do it for every peer.

We checked each fix against the published PyPI wheels, and all five records are updated with the fixed version, the fix commit and the release:
|          Record           |       Package        |    Affected    | Fixed | Fix commit  |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-018883 | aimarket-mcp         | 0.1.0 to 0.6.0 | 0.6.1 | d97507c     |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-021807 | aimarket-emporion    | 0.1.0 to 0.4.0 | 0.4.1 | 05c4684     |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-021946 | aimarket-signal-hunt | 0.1.0 to 0.1.1 | 0.1.2 | 214ee8e     |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-020712 | aimarket-hestia      | 0.1.0 to 0.1.1 | 0.1.2 | cd85ea8     |
| GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-004375 | aimarket-hub         | 3.0.0 to 3.2.1 | 3.7.0 | none public |

Notes:
- aimarket-hub: your range correction is right. PyPI has no 3.3 to 3.6 releases, so the record now runs from 3.0.0 up to 3.7.0. Up to 3.2.0 only oracle-like peers were followed; from 3.2.1 every peer was. The public repo has no single fix commit, so the record links the 3.7.0 release.
- aimarket-hestia: the description now covers the wider scope you described: the restore at boot, the owner update that rewrote the right, and the single owners.code_right rule in 0.1.2.
- aimarket-mcp: a reverse proxy on the same host that adds no forwarding headers still reaches a keyless 0.6.1 server. The record now advises setting AIMARKET_MCP_KEY behind a proxy.
- New record: the NAT64 guard you added to capture.py in aimarket-emporion 0.4.2 fixes a separate flaw in emporion 0.4.0 and 0.4.1. It is filed as GCVE-110-VULN-PYPI-2026-000589, fixed in 0.4.2 by 85ad02b, and it cross-references 021946.

The updated files will appear in this repository with the next publish run, within 6 hours.

Thank you for updating the five records after checking the wheels (and you are right on aimarket-hub: 3.2.0 still followed only oracle-like peers, every peer only from 3.2.1; our comment had 3.2.0 wrong), for widening the hestia description, and for filing the NAT64 gap in aimarket-emporion 0.4.0–0.4.1 as its own record (GCVE-110-VULN-PYPI-2026-000589): agreed, and it is fixed in 0.4.2. Thank you as well for reviewing the three later records by hand. You were right on all three.

The three later records. The fixes are released:

GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-021897, helios-broadcast 0.2.1. Uploads are always private; helios approve (or an operator’s auto-approve) is the only way a video becomes public, and queue ingest drops a requested privacy and logs that it did.
GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-021896, skopos-fleet. The host-key part was already closed in 0.2.0 (RejectPolicy against SKOPOS’s own known_hosts; 0.1.0–0.1.4 accepted any key). The lockout is fixed in 0.2.1: it keys on the websocket’s own peer, trusts proxy headers only from the local proxy, and adds an all-addresses failed-login budget. 0.2.1 also stops the remediation git push from accepting any SSH host key.
GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-022091, aimarket-histor 0.4.1 (0.4.0 was never published). The trace runtime records rename/renameat2/link/linkat/symlink/symlinkat/creat and judges their targets like writes; .pth and sitecustomize files outside /tmp, and code written into the installed package after install, are reported as persistence; a trace runtime missing any of those calls is treated as no trace runtime.
Could you set the fixed versions on these three records (helios-broadcast 0.2.1; skopos-fleet 0.2.0 for the host-key part and 0.2.1 for the lockout, or 0.2.1 for the record as a whole; aimarket-histor 0.4.1)?

GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-018883, the reverse-proxy note. You are right, and we reproduced it against 0.6.2: nginx’s default proxy_pass sends Host: 127.0.0.1:<port> and no forwarding header, so a keyless server behind it answered everyone. aimarket-mcp 0.6.3 adds one more condition on Linux: the caller’s socket must belong to the user the server runs as (the kernel records the owner of each socket in /proc/net/tcp), so a proxy whose workers run as their own user now gets 401. Through nginx in a test container: 200 on 0.6.2, 401 on 0.6.3; the same user connecting directly: 200 on both. A proxy that runs as the server’s own user, or any proxy on macOS or Windows, still looks local, so the README now says to set AIMARKET_MCP_KEY behind any reverse proxy, as your record advises. Three other packages of ours used the same keyless rule and have the same check now (aimarket-metis 0.2.3, aimarket-platon 0.1.5, aimarket-treasury 0.1.3).

GCVE-110-VULN-PYPI-2026-000504, aimarket-hestia 0.1.1 (dynamic code execution). We think this one is a false positive and would ask you to withdraw it. The flagged line, exec(compile(request["source"], "handler.py", "exec"), namespace) in hestia/sandbox.py, is never run by the host process. It is part of GUEST, a string passed as python -c to CPython compiled to WASI, which wasmtime runs in a fresh instance for every call (Sandbox.run, wasi.argv = [..., "-c", GUEST]). Running a tenant’s handler is what HESTIA is for; the question is where it runs. The instance sees the standard library read-only at /lib and nothing else of the filesystem, has no sockets (WASI preview 1), no processes and two fixed environment variables, and runs under a memory ceiling, an epoch deadline and a cap on what it may write back; signing keys stay outside. The same code is in 0.1.1, 0.1.2 and 0.1.3. Which keys may run code outside this sandbox at all is the owner rule you recorded as GCVE-110-PYPI-2026-020712 (fixed in 0.1.2: an open-signup key runs code only here).

Your findings also sent us looking for the same mistakes elsewhere in our code. We found more cases of four of these kinds (a server open when no key is set, checking an address and then connecting by name, trusting a caller’s proxy headers, SSH host keys), fixed them and released the fixes, among them the emporion guard you filed.

Thanks again.
